themes.label: Inventories
themes.rationale: The inscription is a detailed inventory of naval equipment belonging to the Athenian state, listing specific items like masts, oars, and rudders for various triremes.

themes.label: Accounts and Financial Records
themes.rationale: These naval lists served as official accounts for the curators of the dockyards, tracking the responsibility of trierarchs and the status of captured military equipment.

themes.label: Stele
themes.rationale: The inscription is recorded on a stone slab, which was the standard format for public administrative records in 4th-century Athens.

themes.label: Marble
themes.rationale: The material used for Athenian public inscriptions of this period was typically Pentelic marble.

themes.label: Fragmentary
themes.rationale: The text contains numerous lacunae and restored sections, indicating the stone is not fully preserved.

themes.label: Damnatio Memoriae-like Name Erasure
themes.rationale: The word for 'general' (strategos) is enclosed in double brackets, indicating an intentional erasure or modification on the stone, likely following the political downfall of the individuals mentioned.

rationale: This inscription belongs to the Athenian Naval Catalogues, specifically recording the equipment (skeue) of triremes in the year 374/3 BC. It lists various types of oars (thranite, zygian, thalamian), masts, and rudders. A significant historical feature is the mention of ships captured (aichmalotos) during the campaigns of the famous generals Timotheus and Chabrias. The ship names mentioned include Panthera, Galateia, Nemesis, Euploia, Genesis, and Demokratia. The erasure of the title 'strategos' reflects the volatile political status of these military leaders in Athens.
